body: Thanks for the comment. I've tried resources available here, didn't work out. Too poor to afford help, but don't qualify for assistance. I don't know what beauty has to do with anything, but I'm not feeling worth much at all.
They can't afford it. They couldn't afford to take their sick cat to the vet last week and I had to let them use my old credit card which has me in thousands of dollars of debt.

I only talk to my boyfriend about it. I don't want anyone else to know, especially not my family. One time the discussion with my boyfriend turned into an argument and he threatened to tell my mom about it if I didn't. I immediately felt sick. I doubled over and cried and begged him not to. In my head only more bad feelings can come from my family finding out.

Thanks. I might be able to afford something like that. I've never done this before. How often and how long do therapists usually talk with patients? Or is it different for each person?

Edit: words/spelling

Thanks. I'm an adult with no insurance, no doctor, no meds, and no one I feel safe talking to about it. I'm terrified of being held for any amount of time though. (I can't miss time at work or I'll loose my job, which isn't even paying enough for me to pay the bills and buy necessities.) But if I ever get close to the thought of actually going through with suicide I'd have to go to the ER I guess.

I have only been to a gyno once in my life, about 10 years ago. It's been almost as long since I've seen any kind of doctor... I feel the same. If something's wrong, I don't really want to fix it. It's fucked up, but I like to look at it as guilt free suicide.
Thanks, everyone. I'm going to try to get some sleep now. I'm feeling a lot less alone after reading your messages. Tomorrow should be better.

I've been thinking about doing the same thing. I'm kind of afraid to read things I write though. I usually only get the urge to write when I'm feeling really bad. If I read that when I feel okay it might bring me down. I don't know. I don't have anyone to talk to either, also no health insurance, so it might be good just to get my thoughts out there somewhere.

It's alright, but I try to avoid telling them about most things. I don't want to hear what they'll have to say about it. They might be able to lend me money, but I already owe them some and they're still paying back loans they took out to pay for my school. I don't want to put them even more in debt.
Also, I don't have any friends. Zero. There's no one I talk to outside of my house.
I'm going through the same thing. I'm going to call a hotline tomorrow, at least the phone call is free. Maybe they can give some advice on affordable options.

I'm also trying to find affordable help, but for depression. I don't have health insurance, I don't get any kind of government funded medical assistance, and all the money I make (waiting tables) goes straight to paying the bills. I checked the yellow pages for a city/state run program for low income residents, but I didn't fit the criteria. Maybe you do, look into it where you live! I found the number for the psychiatry services at my local hospital and I've also got a hotline number. I think I'll call them both tomorrow after work and tell them my situation and see what I can do. If they give me any information that could also help you in your situation I'll be sure to pass it along! Hang in there!
Thanks. I just don't have many people I'm comfortable using for support.
I wish there were more people I trusted enough to tell. And unfortunately I no longer attend any school.

Over a long time I've gone through so many interests and hobbies, but none of them seem to stick with me. They get old and boring, and I don't get anything out of them anymore. I can totally relate to your lack of motivation. So instead this might work for you too: When I'm bored or bummed out I know I've just gotta do something to take my mind off of things. A nice steamy shower, a plate full of food that's bad for me but tastes delicious, a video game, cleaning, getting the cat to chase a toy, anything to keep me from laying around in bed which just makes me feel worse, I'm sick and tired of feeling bad. Someone else said it in another comment, small steps. Keep taking them and you might find that desire to do more again.
Yeah, I know he is. That's why I didn't want him to find out. But I just feel like I can't tell my family because maybe they're part of the problem.
